blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine peso weakened past the 64-per-dollar level for the first time on Tuesday, extending its record-breaking slide as investors braced for a busy week of major central bank decisions. At the same time, concerns over the domestic economy’s growth outlook and persistent inflation linger. The currency touched an intraday low of 64 against the greenback as of 11:03 a.m., data from the Bankers Association of the Philippines showed.
